description:
## Historical delivery

Commit `ca10f62f9` added explicit correlated parameter/result contracts to the previously undeclared private helpers in Enum, Json, Map, and Range, gave `Json.encode!/1` explicit unsupported-value behavior, removed obsolete diagnostics sidecars, and passed the recorded library/fixture/CLI gates.

Those contracts remain useful, truthful source-owned semantic declarations. fz-tfn.58's remaining Enum scope was therefore already complete and is closed as superseded by this ticket.

## Corrected warning premise

The former justification—an undeclared parameter independently means every value must be checked for clause coverage—does not describe the final demand-driven compiler. A clause-coverage warning exists only when an actual demanded typed activation row can reach `Dispatch Fail`. A contract can refine or reject that reached row; it is not an independent coverage universe and an unobserved contract alternative does no work.

fz-kdt.36.1 removes the source-head and whole-contract coverage paths. The contracts delivered here are retained for their semantic/API value, not as warning-suppression annotations.

comments.text: Delivered in ca10f62f9. Added explicit parameter and result domains for all 84 previously undeclared private helpers across Enum, Json, Map, and Range; the fixture matrix now inventories every private helper signature and requires a same-file spec. Json.encode!/1 keeps its public any domain and now has explicit unsupported-value and non-byte-aligned-bitstring panic behavior, both tested through interp, run, and build. Removed 15 diagnostics sidecars made empty by the runtime warning cleanup. Verified 1984 library tests plus 226 runtime tests, 658 fixture-matrix cases, strict workspace/all-target Clippy, 30 CLI tests, AOT variadic coverage, and doctests.

title: The runtime library's clause-coverage warnings are all missing domain declarations
